subject: Request: Subprocessor impact heatmap & minimum evidence for TransitEdge onboarding
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: alice.mason@finserve.com, security@finserve.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Subprocessor impact heatmap & minimum evidence for TransitEdge onboarding

Hi Alice / FinServe security team,

Thanks for the intro call earlier — good to align on scope. As we progress with TransitEdge (the proposed transit/egress partner), Legal and Security have asked for a compact "impact heatmap" that ties the vendor's processing roles to (a) where customer data transits/stays, (b) the minimal evidence set we need for SOC2/DPA review, and (c) whether there are any exportability or residency flags.

Attached is a one-tab template (processor_heatmap_v1.xlsx) — can you fill the yellow columns for:
- Geographic egress (countries/regions)
- Data types touching the processor (logs, metrics, payloads)
- Retention windows and whether the partner can purge on request
- Encryption in transit + at rest (KMS/HSM involvement)
- Any subprocessors they use (names + country)

Minimal evidence requested: SOC 2 summary, encryption attestation, sample audit log snippet showing an export, and DPA addendum sign-off. If they have an existing contractual clause that restricts cross-border transfers, flag it.

Target: can you return the completed heatmap + SOC2 summary by EOD Friday (2027-03-12)? Our Compliance committee meets Tuesday and we'd like to include TransitEdge in the packet if there are no high residuals.

Thanks — cc'ing Kimberly and Jonas from our onboarding and security teams for visibility.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: processor_heatmap_v1.xlsx
From: Alice Mason <alice.mason@finserve.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@finserve.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor impact heatmap & minimum evidence for TransitEdge onboarding

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — happy to help. TransitEdge confirmed they are SOC 2 Type II (report summary attached) and use KMS for at-rest keys; they also have an HSM-backed signing flow for token exchange. I've attached their SOC summary (transitedge-soc2-summary.pdf).

A couple of clarifications:
- "Data types": TransitEdge handles routing metadata and transient payloads (streaming audio transcripts in a minority of flows). They do not persist full user content beyond 48 hours unless needed for debugging (and then only with encryption).
- "Subprocessors": They use "LogSmith" (US) for short-term log buffering and "EdgeMirror" (IE) for regional caching.
- Exportability: They operate a EU region and a US region. Cross-border exports occur for centralized telemetry; they claim contractual safeguards and SCCs in place but can provide evidence.

We will populate your heatmap and return the files by Thursday COB (2027-03-11) to give you a bit more time to correlate with the SOC summary.

Best,
Alice Mason
Vendor Ops — FinServe

Attachments: transitedge-soc2-summary.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com, alice.mason@finserve.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor impact heatmap & minimum evidence for TransitEdge onboarding

Naomi / Alice — thanks for the fast turnaround. Couple quick internal asks so we can sign off: 

1) Please confirm whether TransitEdge's 48-hour debug retention applies to plain-text transcripts or only encrypted blobs. If plaintext, we need to see the purge workflow and a sample API deletion call.
2) For LogSmith (US) and EdgeMirror (IE), we need a short statement of whether those subprocessors are contractually authorized in TransitEdge's DPA and whether they keep additional backups beyond the 48-hour window.
3) For cross-border telemetry exports: we need a short dataflow sentence and one log sample (redacted) showing the egress path (timestamps + IP blocks are fine).

Connor — looping you for the limited-scope escrow alternative: if TransitEdge cannot provide immediate log samples due to retention policy, can we request a temporary escrowed snapshot under NDA for our audit? If so, we'll include the escrow workflow in the evidence pack.

Naomi — I'll draft a minimal DPA addendum (only the Transfer + Subprocessor paragraphs) and attach a DocuSign link once Alice confirms the pieces above.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi all — attaching an updated heatmap with Kim's review items filled where possible.

Key notes in the sheet:
- TransitEdge marks transcripts as encrypted at rest; plaintext trimming occurs at 48h but debug retention may be plaintext for a narrow subset (requires escrow request).
- LogSmith retention: 7 days with a limited backup snapshot for incident response; EdgeMirror holds cache shards for up to 14 days in EU nodes.
- We recommend a limited DPA addendum requiring: encrypted storage enforcement, immediate purge on customer request, and an escrow snapshot only under NDA + court/jurisdiction limitations.

Alice — can you confirm by EOD whether FinServe will sign the addendum? If yes, Kimberly will send the DocuSign link and we can close the onboarding items.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Security Engineering (on behalf of Compliance)
Redwood Inference
